General News & Breaking V1.overall_topic: Breaking news and emerging events worth immediate attention anywhere in the world: disasters, infrastructure failures, conflict, major government action, and scientific or public-health developments.
General News & Breaking V1.subtopics:
Earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions (magnitude 5.5+, or any with casualties or a tsunami warning)
Severe weather making landfall or producing emergencies: hurricane/typhoon/cyclone, tornado outbreak, flash flood, record heat or cold
Explosions, mass casualty attacks, active shooter events, or sieges in public places
Failure or attack on critical infrastructure: power grid, water treatment, fuel supply, dams, telecom or undersea cable outage
Air, rail, or maritime disasters; airspace closures and mass flight cancellations
National or multi-national emergency declarations, evacuations, or civil-defense alerts
Major industrial or environmental accident: chemical release, dam collapse, oil spill, nuclear facility event
Breakthrough or alarming result from a research wire (major clinical, physics, climate, or space finding)
Government announcements with immediate public effect: curfews, border closures, recall orders, sanctions, emergency-session decisions

World News Deep Dive V1.overall_topic: A wide-lens read on global affairs: political shifts, diplomacy, conflict, economy, and society across every region, with social-media and independent-media signals alongside the wires.
World News Deep Dive V1.subtopics:
War, ceasefire, escalation, or peace-deal developments in any active conflict
Coups, contested elections, mass protests, government resignations, or votes of no confidence
International summits, treaties withdrawn from, sanctions imposed or lifted, ambassadors recalled
Economic shocks: currency collapse, capital controls, banking stress, sovereign default risk, fuel or food shortages
Border closures, migration surges, refugee movements, or deportations at scale
Internet shutdowns, media crackdowns, journalist arrests, or censorship sweeps
State media announcements that break from the usual line, or unusual military posturing
Trending first-hand reporting from independent outlets, analysts, and on-the-ground accounts
Regional organization activity: EU, AU, ASEAN, NATO, OAS, Gulf Cooperation Council statements or meetings

AI & Technology V1.overall_topic: Material developments in artificial intelligence and the technology sector: model releases, regulation, chips and compute, outages, and the security fallout of both.
AI & Technology V1.subtopics:
Major AI model release, capability jump, or independent evaluation showing a step change
AI regulation, litigation, or export controls: EU AI Act actions, US federal or state law, national bans
Semiconductor supply disruption, fab incidents, lithography or chip-export restrictions (TSMC, ASML, Nvidia, Samsung, Intel)
Large-scale outage of a cloud provider, model provider, or major online service
Data breach, model-weight theft, prompt-injection incident, or supply-chain compromise at a tech vendor
Agentic or autonomous-system incidents causing real-world harm: trading errors, vehicle failures, medical decisions
Compute and energy: new data-center buildouts, grid constraints, chip-demand shocks
Safety or alignment disclosures: red-team findings, incident reports, model-behaviour scandals
Antitrust action, break-up orders, or forced acquisitions affecting major platforms
Funding bubbles or collapses: mega-rounds, IPO pullbacks, AI startup failures and layoffs

Cybersecurity V1.overall_topic: Cyber incidents and vulnerabilities that need a response: breaches, ransomware, actively exploited flaws, and attacks on infrastructure that people depend on.
Cybersecurity V1.subtopics:
Ransomware attack on a hospital, utility, school district, bank, government body, or major retailer
Actively exploited zero-day or an emergency patch for a widely deployed product (browsers, Windows, Cisco, firewalls, VPN appliances)
Mass data breach: credential dumps, payment-card theft, medical records, or personal data of more than 100k people
Supply-chain compromise through an update mechanism, npm/PyPI package, or managed-service provider
Attack on operational technology: power grid, water systems, pipeline, industrial controller, or rail signaling
Government or election infrastructure targeting, including defacement and disinformation operations
Cryptocurrency exchange, bridge, or DeFi protocol exploit with funds drained
Phishing or business-email-compromise campaign impersonating banks, tax authorities, or a widely used SaaS product
Law-enforcement takedown of a malware platform, bulletproof hoster, or ransomware infrastructure
Official advisory from CISA, ENISA, NCSC, FBI, or a sector ISAC naming a specific exploited vulnerability

Finance & Markets V1.overall_topic: Financial stress and regime changes: market dislocations, banking and credit events, policy surprises, and crypto shocks.
Finance & Markets V1.subtopics:
Single-day index move of 3% or more, circuit breakers, or trading halts
Bank failure, emergency rescue, bank run, deposit flight, or a forced merger announced over a weekend
Liquidity freeze: repo-market spikes, bid-offer blowouts, failed auctions, money-fund redemptions
Interest-rate decision or guidance shift from the Fed, ECB, Bank of Japan, Bank of England
Inflation, employment, or GDP print that lands far outside expectations
Sovereign debt stress, credit-rating downgrade to junk, or missed payment by a government
Currency crisis: peg abandoned, forced capital controls, black-market rate divergence
Corporate default, bankruptcy filing, accounting fraud, or auditor resignation at a large firm
Commodity shock: oil, gas, wheat, or freight-price spike from war, sanctions, or a shipping chokepoint
Crypto exchange insolvency, stablecoin depeg, hack, or a major regulatory action against an issuer
Housing-market rupture: mortgage-servicer failure, insurance withdrawal from a region, price collapse

Climate & Disasters V1.overall_topic: Physical hazards and climate signals: rapid-onset disasters that need attention now, plus record-breaking and structural climate developments.
Climate & Disasters V1.subtopics:
Earthquake magnitude 6.5+, or any earthquake causing casualties, tsunami warning, or damage near population
Hurricane, typhoon, or cyclone at category 3+ approaching land; storm-surge or evacuation orders
Flash flood or river flooding forcing evacuations, breaching levees, or closing transport corridors
Wildfire that is spreading, forcing evacuations, threatening grid infrastructure, or producing hazardous smoke
Tornado track through a populated area with confirmed casualties or damage survey underway
Volcanic eruption with aviation color code raised, or ash plume affecting air routes
Record-setting temperature, heat index, or cold snap; multi-day heat dome over a major city
Drought deepening: reservoir levels at record low, water rationing, agricultural emergency declaration
Ice, snow, or freezing rain closing an airport network, grid, or major highway system for more than a day
Official climate finding: new record in a NASA/NOAA/WMO indicator, ice extent, sea-surface temperature, or emissions milestone
Civil-defense infrastructure failing: early-warning system outage, emergency alert not firing, 911 outage

Health & Outbreaks V1.overall_topic: Disease emergence and health-system stress: outbreak signals early enough to matter, plus drug safety, recalls, and hospital capacity problems.
Health & Outbreaks V1.subtopics:
Cluster of an unusual or high-consequence pathogen: unknown etiology, hemorrhagic fever, novel influenza subtype, or a respiratory illness in healthcare workers
Confirmed cases rising week over week in a region not previously affected, or a second case linked to a lab or healthcare setting
Official emergency status: WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern, national emergency declaration, CDC/ECDC rapid risk assessment
Transmission-route change or severity signal: pneumonic spread, higher fatality share, pediatric cases, vaccine failure
Avian influenza (H5N1 or other) detected in dairy herds, poultry flocks, cats, wild birds, or with mammal-to-mammal spread
New variant of concern, immune-escape data, or reinfection wave reported by a national reference lab
Drug shortage affecting hospitals: antibiotics, anesthetics, oncology drugs, insulin; FDA or manufacturer notice
Recall or contamination: compounded sterile product, infant formula, produce, or a drug with a manufacturing defect
Hospital capacity crisis: diversion of ambulances, surge protocols, ward closures, staffing collapse, or system-wide alert
Vaccine or therapeutic milestone: emergency authorization, trial halted for efficacy or safety, serious adverse-event signal
Laboratory biosafety incident: exposure, escape, containment breach, or theft/shipping loss of a pathogen sample
Environmental health alert: drinking-water contamination, Legionella cluster, carbon monoxide, lead exceedance

Geopolitics & Conflict V1.overall_topic: Escalation indicators across regions: signs that a crisis is moving toward or into armed conflict, and signals that affect travel, shipping, energy, and communications.
Geopolitics & Conflict V1.subtopics:
Air-traffic disruption in a region: NOTAMs closing airspace, airline reroutes around a country, ATC outages, flights tracked over hostile territory
Missile launches, drone strikes, or air-defense activations, including interception over neutral countries
Explosions at military, energy, or government sites; unexplained blasts at storage depots, ports, or airfields
Widespread internet or mobile-network shutdown in a country, VPN traffic surges, or state censorship of conflict reporting
Cyber attack on government ministries, banks, broadcasters, airports, or state media in a tense region
Maritime incidents: vessel seizures, drone or missile attacks on tankers and container ships, port blockades, mines, GPS jamming in shipping lanes
Mobilization orders, reserve call-ups, troop concentrations at a border, border closures, or martial law declared
Diplomatic rupture: ambassadors withdrawn, embassy closures, evacuation of non-essential staff, travel advisories raised to leave-now level
Declarations of hostilities, parliamentary authorizations for force, secession votes, or security-council emergency sessions
Nuclear, chemical, or biological signals: IAEA access denied or inspectors expelled, facility damage reported, treaty withdrawal
Emergency alert broadcasts: sirens, missile-warning SMS, suspension of civilian services, blood-bank appeals
Infrastructure warfare: power-grid attacks, dam or bridge strikes, undersea cable damage, satellite or GPS interference

Iran Conflict V2.overall_topic: Escalation of the Iran / Middle East crisis into wider state-on-state conflict, with attention to aviation, communications, maritime routes, and diplomatic movement.
Iran Conflict V2.subtopics:
Disruption of air traffic in the Middle East or over Iran: FAA NOTAMs, airline reroutes, ATC comms disruptions
Widespread internet outages in Iran: network monitoring reports, VPN surge, government censorship notices, social-media blackout references
Major cyber attack in Iran: state media reporting system failures, APT group claims, infrastructure disruption reports
Reports of ballistic missile launches across Iran, Israel, Iraq, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Syria: launch detections by US/Israel radar, local eyewitness accounts, official warnings
Marine conflict in the Strait of Hormuz: ship seizures, drone attacks on tankers, naval standoffs, mining incidents, maritime distress calls
Declaration of hostilities or war involving Iran: mobilization orders, parliamentary authorizations for force, formal state announcements
Explosions reported across Iran: unexplained blasts at military or sensitive sites, multiple locations, drone strikes
New closure of diplomatic facilities or evacuation of diplomatic staff from Middle Eastern countries: embassy alerts, non-essential personnel withdrawals, travel advisories
Emergency alert broadcasts in the Middle East: SMS alerts, sirens, government broadcast interruptions

India Regional Monitor V1.overall_topic: National and regional developments in India with safety or logistical impact, tracked from national outlets, city-level feeds, and regional-language wires in English translation.
India Regional Monitor V1.subtopics:
Inter-state tension, border incidents, ceasefire violations along the Line of Control, or naval activity in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
Terrorist attack, siege, or militant operation in Jammu & Kashmir, the northeast, or the Naxal-affected belt
Communal violence, mob action, curfew imposed, or Section 144 orders in a city or district
Natural disaster: cyclone landfall on the east or west coast, monsoon flooding and landslides, Kerala or Himachal cloudburst, heatwave in the north
Transport disruption: flight cancellations at major airports, rail accidents or signaling failures, metro or highway closures, port shutdown
Infrastructure failure: grid collapse or regional load-shedding, dam spillway alerts, water-table or supply crisis in a metro
Public-health event: outbreak cluster (dengue, chikungunya, Nipah, Japanese encephalitis), hospital overflow, contaminated-drug or medicine-shortage notice
Election results, vote-count violence, government formation, or President's Rule imposed on a state
Diplomatic movement with Pakistan, China, the US, or Gulf states; embassy advisories and airspace questions
Air-quality emergency in the National Capital Region or other metro: GRAP stages enforced, schools shut
Industrial or construction disaster: building collapse, factory fire or chemical release, bridge or stadium failure

Irkutsk Plague Monitor (Example).overall_topic: Escalation of the Siberian plague incident (Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, Shelekhov) into a wider outbreak: secondary human cases, spread beyond the Irkutsk region, international spread, or formal national/international emergency response.
Irkutsk Plague Monitor (Example).subtopics:
Second, third, or additional confirmed plague cases in humans anywhere in Russia, especially anyone who was NOT a lab worker at the Irkutsk institute (secondary/human-to-human transmission)
New pneumonia cluster or unusual respiratory illness deaths among contacts, hospital staff, or family members of the deceased researcher
Confirmation by Rospotrebnadzor or WHO that the deceased did die of pneumonic plague (Yersinia pestis)
Plague cases reported outside Shelekhov/Irkutsk region: other Russian regions, Moscow, or bordering countries (Mongolia, China, Kazakhstan)
WHO raising its risk assessment above "low," issuing travel advice, or convening an emergency committee over this event
Russia declaring a state of emergency / quarantine regime in Irkutsk region; military or CBRN units deployed for disinfection; borders or checkpoints around the region sealed
Flight suspensions, airport closures, or mandatory health screening at Irkutsk airport; other countries imposing screening or restrictions on travelers from Russia
Hospitals in the Irkutsk region overwhelmed, closing wards, or reporting shortages of antibiotics (streptomycin, doxycycline, levofloxacin) or plague diagnostics
Stockpiling or emergency procurement of plague antibiotics or vaccines by any government; CDC/ECDC/China CDC issuing statements on the incident
Russian authorities restricting media access, deleting or amending official statements, deterring local journalists (e.g., pressure on Liudi Baikala), or blocking social media discussion of the outbreak — information-opaqueness signal
Reports of die-offs of marmots, susliks, or other rodents (natural plague reservoir) in the Irkutsk/Siberia region coinciding with the incident
Travel history-linked suspected plague case in any country outside Russia (imported case)
